title: What a score can carry
summary: Independent revision on measurement in personality: three short activities on reliability, reversed items and response styles, each followed by a written answer to check against the notes.
author: Open Psychology Interactives
intro:
Revision for the measurement part of the personality module. Work through the three activities in order; each takes about six minutes. Write your answers as if you were explaining them to someone who has not seen the activities.

Nothing you type is sent anywhere. Download or copy your answers at the end and check them against your notes.

steps.instructions: Predict before you open the scale. Then raise the number of near-duplicate items and watch alpha, the content the ten items cover, and the correlation with the outcome move together.

steps.prompt: In two sentences: what does a high alpha tell you, and what does it not tell you?

steps.instructions: Both reverse-keyed items start unrecoded. Repair the first and note alpha. Then repair the second and note it again.

steps.prompt: Repairing the first reversed item barely moved alpha; repairing the second moved it a lot. Explain the mechanism without using the word "error".

steps.instructions: Predict which of the four respondents balanced keying will rescue. Then switch between the balanced and the unbalanced questionnaire and compare each recoded score with the score their true standing implies.

steps.prompt: Name one response style, say what it does to a total score, and say why balanced keying rescues one style and leaves the others untouched.
